design_condition: The new volume straddles the perimeter of the historic enclosure, extending its orthogonal geometry and height to mediate between the historic complex and the surrounding urban fabric.

positive.statement: The compact urban-planning approach and recomposition of the closed orthogonal structure are convincing.
The new building precisely adopts the geometry and height of its surroundings, achieving suitable volumetric interaction.
The division between service spaces toward the city and living spaces toward the historic roofs is appreciated.
The room organization and thresholds are efficient.
New trees connect existing green areas and provide effective shading to the south-facing façade.
The water feature is a valuable fixed furnishing element in the outdoor spaces.

negative.statement: The lack of continuity in the ground-floor public spaces weakens the clarity of the urban layout.
The internal empty spaces, pedestrian paths, transparencies, and greenery should have been better defined.
Residual spaces outside the enclosure lack a stronger spatial and functional connotation.
The accesses to the building and site lack the necessary depth, clarity, and generosity.
The rigid wall creates excessive closure and limited permeability toward the city.
The architectural language is too abstract and impersonal, and its dual identity is not convincing.
The common living spaces lack generosity despite the use of double heights.
The interventions within the historic structure remain insufficiently thorough and evasive.
The load-descent system and resistance to horizontal forces require improvement and verification.
The effect of the glazed northern façade on energy needs requires verification.
The sustainability impacts of the materials are not explicitly mentioned.
